description: Selector strategy for Playwright test generation. Automation Agent reads this to decide how to locate elements.

verificationRequired.rule: count MUST be a MEASURED value returned by actually executing the locator against the live DOM — NEVER a value typed/assumed by the agent. Before recording evidence, run the selector and read back the real match count.
howToMeasure: Playwright MCP: run `browser_evaluate` with `document.querySelectorAll('<css-equivalent>').length`, OR for getBy* locators evaluate the equivalent DOM query and read `.length`.
Local dry-run: `await page.locator(<selector>).count()` and read the returned integer.
The number written into evidence.count is the number the tool RETURNED — if the tool was not run, there is NO evidence and the selector is rejected.
verificationRequired.verifiedByField: evidence.verifiedBy records HOW count was measured: 'browser_evaluate' | 'locator.count()' | 'page-snapshot-match'. A missing or 'assumed'/'manual' verifiedBy = unverified = rejected.
verificationRequired.antiHallucination: Writing count:1 without having executed the locator is a hard violation (self-reported evidence). The measured count is the single source of truth — the schema value only mirrors what the tool returned.

patterns: comma-separated selectors (multiple selectors in one string)

fallbackStrategy.approach: Generate primary + up to 2 fallback selectors per element upfront, chained with Playwright .or() at runtime. EVERY selector in the chain — primary AND each fallback — must be independently verified against the live DOM at generation time with its own evidence (source + count === 1). An unverified fallback is a guess, not a fallback, and is banned.

evidenceForEveryLink.rule: Each selector placed in a .or() chain MUST have been discovered via DOM inspection and resolve to exactly ONE element (count === 1) at generation time. Record evidence per selector in the manifest locator entry.
evidenceForEveryLink.rationale: .or() binds to the FIRST matching selector. If a fallback is unverified or non-unique, the chain can silently bind to the WRONG element and report a false pass. Every link must be as proven as the primary.
evidenceForEveryLink.banned: Selectors added 'from memory' or 'by common pattern' as fallbacks without DOM evidence. If you cannot verify a fallback resolves to count === 1, do NOT add it.

fallbackStrategy.implementation: For each interactive element, discover 2-3 real selectors from the DOM (each unique). Chain the top two with .or() in the Page Object; the third stays as an evidence-tagged comment. All are backed by discovery evidence — none invented.
rules: Generate at least 2 evidence-backed selectors per interactive element (each verified count === 1)
Use .or() to chain primary and first fallback in the Page Object
Third selector stays as an evidence-tagged comment for manual fix if both fail
Runtime preference: an evidence-backed fallback in the chain is used automatically by .or() — cheap, no MCP call, and SAFE because it was verified at generation time
Escalate to DOM re-inspection (Playwright MCP) ONLY when the ENTIRE evidence-backed chain fails (element genuinely moved/removed) — that is the one case where the MCP cost is justified

runtimeVsGeneration.generationTime: Every selector (primary + fallbacks) is verified count === 1 against the live DOM before being committed. No unverified selector enters a chain.
runtimeVsGeneration.runtime: Prefer the evidence-backed .or() chain (no MCP needed — cheaper than a browser round-trip). Only when ALL links in the chain fail do you re-inspect the DOM with MCP and regenerate the selector with fresh evidence.

instabilitySurfacing.rule: If, during local validation, the primary selector fails and the run only passes because a fallback caught it, the element's primary is UNSTABLE. Do NOT hide this.
instabilitySurfacing.action: Record the element in the manifest validation.needsReview[] (or an unstableSelectors[] note) with reason 'primary selector failed; passed on fallback — primary needs re-inspection', so drift surfaces instead of silently accumulating rot.
instabilitySurfacing.neverSilent: A test that only passed because of a fallback is a yellow signal, never a clean green.

dryRunFailureHandling.step1: Check if an evidence-backed fallback from the chain resolves (no MCP needed — it was verified at generation time).
dryRunFailureHandling.step2: If a fallback works, promote it to primary in the Page Object AND flag the element as unstable (instabilitySurfacing).
dryRunFailureHandling.step4: If the ENTIRE evidence-backed chain fails, re-inspect the DOM with Playwright MCP, regenerate the selector(s) with fresh count === 1 evidence, and update the Page Object.

massSelectorFailureRecovery.trigger: A large fraction of tests in the run fail with 'locator resolved to 0 elements' / 'strict mode violation' (page changed wholesale, not one selector).
massSelectorFailureRecovery.action: Do NOT patch selectors one by one and do NOT rely on grid autoHeal. Route back to the Automation skill to RE-INSPECT the affected pages with Playwright MCP and REGENERATE the Page Objects with fresh evidence. This writes real, evidence-backed fixes to disk (persistent), unlike a runtime heal.
massSelectorFailureRecovery.autoHeal: Grid-level autoHeal stays DISABLED (it does not modify the script, produces no evidence, and reports a silent pass). Recovery is always via evidence-based regeneration.
